work_order.approach:
Delete the advance; consume occurrences per occurrence. This is the alternative v1 listed first and rejected as "the larger change" — it is larger, and it is also the only one that satisfies AC-2.

1. Server (`server/schedules/app.ts`): keep `postTransactionForSchedule({ id, date, today })` accepting an explicit occurrence date and keep stamping `schedule_occurrence: today ? next_date : (date ?? next_date)`. Remove `advanceScheduleToDate` entirely and revert `setNextDate` to its main-branch shape (drop the `nextDate` parameter and its `nextDate ?? ...` expression — no caller will need it once the advance is gone). `postTransactionForSchedule` no longer touches `next_date` at all.

2. Register preview (`shared/schedules.ts`): give `computeSchedulePreviewTransactions` an optional fifth parameter `postedTransactionsBySchedule?: Map<string, PostedScheduleTransaction[]>`, defaulting to an empty Map. After the forward generation and the existing `status === 'paid'` shift, drop every remaining date for which `isScheduleOccurrencePosted({ schedule, scheduleId, occurrenceDate, postedTransactions })` is true. Do NOT delete the `dates.shift()`: it covers the unstamped-legacy case where `getHasTransactionsQuery`'s lower-bound arm matched a transaction dated after the occurrence, which `isScheduleOccurrencePosted`'s two-sided window deliberately does not match. Keep both.

3. New query builder `getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery(schedules)`: every transaction carrying one of the given `schedule` ids, selecting `['schedule','date','schedule_occurrence']`, `.options({ splits: 'all' })`, with the same `{ id: null }` no-match guard for an empty list. This is a NEW function — do not widen `getHasTransactionsQuery`, which is load-bearing for `hasTransactionForSchedule` and `advanceSchedulesService`: broadening it would make a later posted occurrence mark an earlier one paid, which is BUG-1 again, in the auto-post path.

4. Plumbing: `hooks/useSchedules.ts` opens a second live query over `getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery(schedules)`, indexes with `indexPostedScheduleTransactions`, exposes `postedTransactionsBySchedule` on `ScheduleData` (hence `UseSchedulesResult`, which is the context value type, so `useCachedSchedules` needs no edit), tearing it down alongside `statusQueryRef` in both the re-subscribe path and the unmount cleanup. `hooks/usePreviewTransactions.ts` passes it through as the fifth argument.

5. BUG-2, in the same handler: when `!today`, before `addTransactions`, query for an existing transaction with this `schedule` id and this `schedule_occurrence`; if one exists, return without writing. The handler is a mutator and mutators are `sequential`, so this is race-safe against concurrent dispatch. Guard only the `!today` path: `today` deliberately discharges `next_date` and can legitimately be invoked more than once, and changing it would move AC-3.

Net behaviour on QA's repro: post 10/10 with 10/03 unpaid → one transaction stamped 10/10 dated 10/10; `next_date` stays 10/03 with status 'due'; previews are 10/03 (Due) + 10/17/10/24/10/31 (Upcoming). 10/03 remains previewed and payable. AC-1 still holds: post 10/02 then 10/09 → two transactions on their own dates, both occurrences consumed by the per-occurrence filter, later occurrences untouched.
assumptions: The `schedule_occurrence` stamp introduced by the earlier work on this issue (commit 9065a36) is present on every transaction this PR creates, and older transactions without it keep working through the unstamped date-comparison fallback — the fix does not depend on a backfill.

`computeSchedulePreviewTransactions` has exactly one production caller (`usePreviewTransactions`), so a fifth positional parameter cannot silently change behaviour elsewhere. Callers that omit it get an empty map and today's behaviour.
`useCachedSchedules`' context value type is `UseSchedulesResult`, so adding a field to the hook result requires no edit in `useCachedSchedules.tsx`.

The `date` sent from the register is always an occurrence of that schedule. `advanceScheduleToDate` used to guard against a date that was not on the recurrence; the new code does not need to, because such a date never matches a generated preview date and so cannot be clicked — but a caller supplying one programmatically would stamp a transaction for an occurrence the schedule never had.
`mutator()` wrapping plus `sequential` means two concurrent `schedule/post-transaction` calls do not interleave, which is what makes the BUG-2 guard safe without a lock.
work_order.confidence_rationale: The mechanism is fully traced and deterministic: the one-deep `dates.shift()` at shared/schedules.ts:532, the `next_date`-only filter in `getHasTransactionsQuery` at line 192, and the advance in app.ts that QA's error-context matches exactly. The replacement mechanism is not invented — it is the per-occurrence dedup `forecast-schedules.ts:205` already runs in production. isScheduleOccurrencePosted falls back to a two-sided date comparison for UNSTAMMED transactions while getHasTransactionsQuery uses only a lower bound. work_order.root_cause: Occurrence consumption and the schedule's `next_date` pointer are the same variable. `computeSchedulePreviewTransactions` (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:473) builds every schedule's preview dates forward from the single `next_date` pointer, and the only way it ever removes one is `if (status === 'paid') dates.shift()` at line 532 — one deep, and gated on `status`, which comes from `getHasTransactionsQuery` (line 192), which only ever asks about `next_date`. The data model therefore has exactly one slot to record "this occurrence is paid": the slot `next_date` points at. Posting occurrence 10/10 while 10/03 is still unpaid requires recording two facts at once — 10/10 paid, 10/03 still owed — and there is nowhere to put the first without destroying the second. `advanceScheduleToDate` is the mechanism that destroys it: it walks `next_date` forward over every occurrence between the old pointer and the posted date, writing nothing for any of them, so each of those occurrences simultaneously (a) stops being previewed, because the preview list starts at the new pointer, and (b) can never be posted, because `getHasTransactionsQuery` only ever asks about `next_date`. Hence BUG-1: the 10/03 Due row vanishes from the register and is unpayable forever. The stamp the PR already writes (`schedule_occurrence: date`) carries precisely the information being thrown away — the schedule system already has the right per-occurrence representation (`isScheduleOccurrencePosted`, `indexPostedScheduleTransactions`), and `forecast-schedules.ts` already uses it; only the register preview path never adopted it.

work_order.understanding:
The previous plan was wrong, and it said so itself. Its `approach` read: "previews are always built from next_date forward ... Posting a later occurrence therefore moves `next_date` past any EARLIER occurrence that was never posted, and that earlier occurrence stops being previewed ... Making posting strictly in order the only way to keep every earlier occurrence visible is a product decision beyond this ticket." It then put `computeSchedulePreviewTransactions` and `isScheduleOccurrencePosted` in `out_of_scope` and shipped `advanceScheduleToDate`. That is not a product decision the ticket declines to make — it is the ticket's own AC-2 ("exactly one occurrence is consumed by the post") being declared out of scope one paragraph after being asserted. QA's T-12 is a faithful reading of AC-2, not a moved goalpost, and it failed for exactly the reason the plan predicted and then declined to fix. BUG-1 is not a missing edge case around `advanceScheduleToDate`; it is the whole design of that helper. v1 also had a coverage blind spot that let it through: its unit test posts occurrence #1 (the schedule's own `next_date`) and then #2, so `next_date` never has to cross an UNPAID occurrence — precisely the only case the new code was wrong in.

What is right in v1 and must survive this rewrite: the `date?` argument threaded from the five client call sites, `parsePreviewId`, and the `schedule_occurrence` stamp. Those are correct and they are the foundation of the real fix — v1 just failed to notice that the stamp alone was enough.

BUG-2 (`schedule/post-transaction` is not idempotent: two messages for the same schedule id + occurrence date create two transactions) is real, reproduces every time, and QA judged it pre-existing rather than introduced. I am fixing it anyway, and the reason is not politeness: the occurrence stamp is the identity this whole ticket is built on, and a handler that can write the same occurrence twice makes that identity meaningless. The fix is three lines, and `schedule/post-transaction` is registered as `mutator(undoable(postTransactionForSchedule))` with `runMutator = sequential(_runMutator)` (packages/loot-core/src/server/mutators.ts:97), so a check-then-write inside the handler body is serialised by construction — the concurrent-double-dispatch case does not need a lock.

I could not execute the failure. `node_modules` is not installed in this checkout (verified twice; node v22.23.3), so no vitest run, no browser, no repro of my own. `reproduced` is therefore false, and what follows is read off the source plus QA's trace and error-context rather than off my own observation.
unknowns: Whether the retained dates.shift() and the new occurrence filter can disagree about a mid-list occurrence for a legacy unstamped transaction. The failure direction (an extra preview row rather than a missing one) is the safe one, but I could not construct the case end to end.

Whether any component outside the register consumes statuses in a way that assumes 'paid' means the head preview is gone. useCachedSchedules is the only context consumer of statuses I traced; I did not audit every getStatus caller.
Whether the per-sync cost of the additional undate-bounded live query is acceptable on a large budget. No measurement was possible without node_modules.

Whether next_date staying on an unpaid occurrence after an out-of-order post changes anything user-visible on the Schedules page beyond the status. AC-7's test covers next_date and status stability; the rendered row was not checked.

review.title: The new duplicate-occurrence guard in postTransactionForSchedule queries q('transactions').filter({ schedule, schedule_occurrence }) with no .options({ splits: 'all' }), so AQL defaults to 'inline' and appends is_parent = 0. A posted occurrence whose transaction has since been split is invisible to the guard and can be written twice, while getHasTransactionsQuery in the same file does pass splits: 'all' and counts that same split parent as paid. The two queries now disagree about whether a split parent's stamp exists.
review.detail:
The new duplicate-occurrence guard in postTransactionForSchedule queries q('transactions').filter({ schedule, schedule_occurrence }) with no .options({ splits: 'all' }), so AQL defaults to 'inline' and appends is_parent = 0. A posted occurrence whose transaction has since been split is invisible to the guard and can be written twice, while getHasTransactionsQuery in the same file does pass splits: 'all' and counts that same split parent as paid. The two queries now disagree about whether a split parent's stamp exists.

`packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:589`

Evidence: packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema/executors.ts:51-53 — const splitType = tableOptions.splits ? tableOptions.splits : 'inline'; and :242-246 — if (splitType !== 'all') { ... s.where = appendWhere(s.where, `${s.from}.is_parent = 0`); }. packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts:33-59 makeChild copies only amount/category/payee/id/account/date/cleared/reconciled/starting_balance_flag/sort_order/is_child/parent_id/error — never schedule or schedule_occurrence — and splitTransaction (:362-391) keeps the original row as the parent with is_parent: true, so the stamp survives only on the row is_parent = 0 excludes. The guard at app.ts:589-591 has no .options(...); getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery (shared/schedules.ts:251-256) and getHasTransactionsQuery (schedules.ts:217-218) both do. Repro: post an occurrence from the register, split that transaction, then dispatch schedule/post-transaction again for the same schedule id and occurrence date — the guard sees no row and writes a second transaction stamped for an already-paid occurrence.

Fix: Add .options({ splits: 'all' }) to the guard query so it matches the same rows getHasTransactionsQuery and getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery match. A broader guard can only ever see more rows, never fewer.

review.title: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions now applies isScheduleOccurrencePosted to every date in the window, which widens the unstamped fallback's 2-day lookback from one occurrence per schedule to every occurrence in the list. UI-created recurring schedules use op: 'isapprox' with posts_transaction: false, so getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns occurrenceDate - 2 days for exactly the schedule kind users create by hand. Where occurrences are one day apart, a single unstamped schedule-linked transaction falls inside three consecutive occurrence windows and silently removes three Upcoming preview rows instead of one.

Where occurrences are one day apart, a single unstamped schedule-linked transaction falls inside three consecutive occurrence windows and silently removes three Upcoming preview rows instead of one.

`packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:596`

Evidence: packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/schedule-edit-utils.ts:49 — updateCond(conds.date, 'isapprox', 'date', fields.date); ScheduleEditModal.tsx:76 seeds _conditions: [{ op: 'isapprox', field: 'date', value: date }] and :53 sets posts_transaction: false. shared/schedules.ts:94-101 — the only two ways to avoid the lookback are dateCond?.op === 'is' and schedule.posts_transaction. shared/schedules.ts:170 — return tx.date >= matchStartDate && tx.date <= occurrenceDate. One-day-apart occurrences are reachable: packages/desktop-client/src/components/select/RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:40 offers { id: 'daily', name: t('Days') }. Unstamped schedule-linked transactions are the norm, not a rarity — packages/loot-core/src/server/rules/action.ts:235-236 is case 'link-schedule': object.schedule = this.value;, which never sets schedule_occurrence, so every rule-matched transaction on a synced budget takes the fallback arm. Before this change only next_date was ever tested, so at most the head could be dropped.

Fix: Narrow the fallback so one transaction discharges at most one occurrence — e.g. match each transaction to the earliest still-unmatched occurrence rather than testing each occurrence against every transaction — or leave multi-day-lookback matching to the status query alone.

review.title: The new publish() closure republishes the whole ScheduleData from either of two independent queries, and both maps are reset to empty on every schedules onData. When the posted-transactions query lands first it publishes schedules paired with an empty statuses, so isForPreview rejects every schedule and the register blanks its Upcoming rows until the slower status query returns. This is a regression on main, which had a single query and could never publish a torn pair.
review.detail:
The new publish() closure republishes the whole ScheduleData from either of two independent queries, and both maps are reset to empty on every schedules onData. When the posted-transactions query lands first it publishes schedules paired with an empty statuses, so isForPreview rejects every schedule and the register blanks its Upcoming rows until the slower status query returns. This is a regression on main, which had a single query and could never publish a torn pair.

`packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:153`

Evidence: In onData (useSchedules.ts:135-191) the two closures are declared `let statuses: ScheduleStatuses = new Map();` and `let postedTransactionsBySchedule = new Map<...>();` (lines 147-151) and publish() (line 153) calls setData({ schedules, statuses, statusLabels, postedTransactionsBySchedule }). Both loadStatuses and loadPostedTransactions are opened synchronously, one after the other (lines 172-190), and whichever resolves first calls publish(). The posted query (getPostedScheduleTransactionsQuery, schedules.ts:232-268) is a plain $or over `schedule: id` selecting three columns; the status query (getHasTransactionsQuery, schedules.ts:192-229) is an $or of per-schedule $and branches each with a second $or and a calculate upstream. The ordering is not merely racy — the cheaper query is expected to win, so the tear is the common case rather than the rare one. On initial mount setIsLoading(false) only fires in the statuses callback (line 178), and usePreviewTransactions gates computeSchedulePreviewTransactions behind isSchedulesLoading (usePreviewTransactions.ts:77-79), so the first load is masked. On a refresh it is not: setIsLoading(true) lives in the effect body (useSchedules.ts:130) keyed on [query, upcomingLength], never in onData, and a schedules onData re-fire is driven by LiveQuery.onUpdate (liveQuery.ts, tables.find(table => this._dependencies.has(table))), i.e. by any sync event touching the schedules table — exactly what advanceSchedulesService and schedule edits produce. At that moment isLoading is already false, so computeSchedulePreviewTransactions runs with an empty status map, isForPreview (schedules.ts:462-471) returns false for every schedule, schedulesForPreview is empty, and usePreviewTransactions sets previewTransactions to []. Balance.tsx:92-95 gates only on isLoading, so the scheduled rows disappear from the register for the round trip and then reappear.

Fix: Do not reset the two maps to empty on refresh. Either seed them from the currently published data before re-opening the queries, or track whether each has reported at least once for this onData and skip publish() until both have. Seeding from the previous snapshot is the smaller change and also avoids the status query's statusLabels map being rebuilt on every posted-transaction event.

qa.title: schedule/post-transaction is not idempotent — posting the same occurrence twice creates two transactions on the same date
qa.expected: Posting one occurrence twice (double-click, or two clients racing) leaves exactly one transaction for that occurrence.
qa.actual: Two concurrent schedule/post-transaction messages for the same schedule id and the same occurrence date create two transactions, both dated on that occurrence. Reproduced on every run of T-10.
repro: Open the preview build and start a fresh local budget.
Create an on-budget account and a weekly +100.00 schedule starting today, with the upcoming window at 30 days.
Issue two schedule/post-transaction messages with the same schedule id and the same future occurrence date, concurrently.
Query the schedule's transactions: there are two, both on that occurrence date.
qa.suspected_cause: postTransactionForSchedule() calls addTransactions() unconditionally; there is no check for an existing transaction carrying the same schedule_occurrence stamp. Judged pre-existing on the source, not on a run: the parent commit's postTransactionForSchedule (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts at 7d50968) has the same unconditional addTransactions and no guard, so double-posting a row produced two transactions before this PR too. This PR does not make it worse — after the first post next_date has already moved to the occurrence, so the second call's advance is a no-op.
